questions.question: / refrigeration.
questions.solution_html:
• Pure cultures can be successfully stored at 40 °C in refrigerators. This method is a short
  • term preservation method. 2-3 weeks for bacteria and 3-4 months for fungi. The
  • metabolic activity of the microorganisms is greatly slowed down but not stopped. Their
  • growth continues slowly as nutrients are utilised and waste products are released into
  • the medium finally results in the death of the microbes after some time.

questions.question: Describe the sterilization controls used to test the effectiveness of a hot air oven. Explain the principle of oil immersion objective in a compound
questions.solution_html:
• Physical, chemical, and biological methods.
  • Physical Controls: monitoring and verifying the operating parameters of the oven –
  • Temperature and time by using thermometers
  • Chemical Indicators: Explain about Browne’s Tube and Chemical Indicator Strips or
  • Tapes.
  • Biological Indicators: The spores of a non-toxigenic strain of Clostridium tetani.
questions.final_answer: Biological Indicators: The spores of a non-toxigenic strain of Clostridium tetani
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: / microscope.
questions.solution_html:
• An oil immersion objective increases the resolving power of a microscope. When light
  • passes from the glass slide (higher refractive index) to air (lower refractive index) and
  • then into the objective lens (higher refractive index), some light is bent away and lost
  • reducing image clarity and brightness. By placing a drop of immersion oil (which has
  • a refractive index similar to that of glass, around 1.5), light rays can pass straight into
  • the objective without significant refraction. More light enters the lens, resulting in a
  • brighter, clearer, and higher-resolution image.
questions.final_answer: brighter, clearer, and higher-resolution image
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write a short note on enriched media with examples.
questions.solution_html:

  • microorganisms that do not grow well on ordinary media. E.g.: Blood agar, chocolate
  • agar, Loeffler’s serum slope, etc.

questions.question: Explain the principle, procedure and types of streak plate method.
questions.solution_html:
• The most common technique of isolation of bacterial cells on the surface of an agar
  • plate is the streaking method. The key principle of this method is that, by streaking, a
  • dilution gradient is established across the surface of the petri plate as bacterial cells are
  • deposited on the agar surface. Each colony is the progeny of a single microbial cell
  • thus
  • representing a clone of pure culture.
  • Principle – ((3 marks))
  • Procedure – ((3 marks))
  • Different methods can be used for streaking. Common ones are the quadrant (four-way
  • streaks), continuous streak and radiant streak methods. ((4 marks))
  • Long Essay Questions
questions.final_answer: Long Essay Questions
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Describe the different types of radiations and filteration techniques used in sterilization.
questions.solution_html:
• Filtration: Helps to remove bacteria from heat-labile liquids such as serum, solution of
  • sugars or antibiotics. Explain the different types of filtrations - Candle filter, Asbestos
  • filter, Sintered glass filter, Membrane filter. ((5 marks))
  • Radiations: Explain the two types. ((5 marks)).
  • Ionising radiation: e.g., X-rays, gamma rays, and high-speed electrons.
  • Non-ionising radiation: e.g. ultraviolet light and infrared light.
questions.final_answer: Non-ionising radiation: e.g. ultraviolet light and infrared light
